questions.cardText:
[History] Which of the following materials was used to make the paint pigment “mummy brown”?
A. A type of dried seaweed that visually resembles a mummy
B. Real mummies
C. Mummified beetles
Answer: B. Ground-up mummies were a popular paint pigment in Europe around the 16th century. Artists prized this pigment for its rich brown hue. Other unconventional uses of mummies included using them as medicine, fertilizer, and even for mummy unwrapping parties.
questions.en: What was the paint pigment “mummy brown” made from?

timeline.labelEn: Mummy brown, made from ground mummies, is popular with European painters
timeline.labelDe: Mumienbraun aus zermahlenen Mumien ist bei europäischen Malern beliebt

questions.notes: CARD ERROR in the explanation: Wikipedia says mummy brown was most popular from the mid-18th to the 19th century (earliest record of sale 1712, demand declined by 1915), not around the 16th century; in the 16th century mummy was used as medicine. The pigment mixed mummy flesh with white pitch and myrrh.

questions.cardText:
[Philosophy] The term “falsifiability” in the philosophy of science refers to:
A. The ability to prove a theory true
B. The ability to prove a theory false
C. The transience nature of scientific theories
Answer: B.
questions.de: Wie heißt der von Karl Popper eingeführte Begriff für die Eigenschaft einer Theorie, durch eine empirische Beobachtung widerlegt werden zu können?
questions.en: What is the term, introduced by Karl Popper, for a theory's capacity to be proven false by an empirical observation?

timeline.labelEn: Karl Popper introduces falsifiability in The Logic of Scientific Discovery
timeline.labelDe: Karl Popper führt die Falsifizierbarkeit in „Logik der Forschung“ ein

questions.notes: Question and answer swapped so the open question has a short answer. Card prints 'transience nature' (sic).
